text:
Maya: We need a new one-pager for the post-webinar drip. Audience: platform security leads + procurement. Goal: concise decision aid comparing Hosted, Dedicated, Private, with two short benchmark callouts and a clear lead routing CTA. Keep it legal-safe and convert-focused.
Tom: I'll build the copy. Suggest 3 stacked panels with a short advice line per panel. Avoid numeric latency claims; link to benchmark hub. Use phrasing like "low p95 latency profiles" and "meaningful unit-cost improvements with batching".
Ivy: Also include a tiny buyer signal checklist so SDRs can triage inbound (e.g., data residency, SLA required, throughput needs). Keep checklist 3 bullets only.
Maya: Great idea. We should use a short URL to our lead routing form (gated) so we can capture intent and route to the right sales lane.
Nate: Compliance checks: 1) No explicit vendor KMS mentions without Legal. 2) "On-prem" ok but remove implication of turnkey air-gapped installs. 3) Add line: "Configurable networking, KMS integrations, and audit logging" is safe.
Compliance-Bot: Reminder: benchmark references must point to Marketing Drive doc ID MD-2024-07 and Ops sign-off required. Add `@ops` to reviewers.
Tom: Draft copy below, please critique.

```
Secure, predictable inference  pick the right deployment for your control needs

Hosted — Fastest path to experimentation
- Benefit: Quick onboarding, API-first hosted inference; ideal for feature validation and early rollouts.
- Security: Shared infrastructure; standard tenant isolation and RBAC controls.
- Buyer signals: prototyping, low compliance requirements.

Dedicated — Predictable capacity & SLAs
- Benefit: Reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling for steady production load.
- Security: Data-isolated capacity and enhanced access controls.
- Buyer signals: need for SLAs, steady throughput.

Private — Full control for regulated workloads
- Benefit: VPC/on-prem deployment options with audit logging and customer KMS integrations.
- Security: Network isolation, custom policies, and longer retention options.
- Buyer signals: data residency or regulatory constraints.

Quick triage (SDR): Data residency? SLA mandatory? Throughput > X? (replace X in form)

Benchmarks: Refer to our benchmark hub (MD-2024-07) for latency profiles by model/region and detailed cost comparisons. Performance varies by model, hardware, and prompt patterns.

Ready to route a lead? Book a deployment review (shortlink: redwood.ai/route) — this will capture buyer signals and route to Dedicated/Private sales lanes.
```

Ivy: Nice. One edit: change the SDR triage line to actionable checkboxes: "Data residency: yes/no | SLA required: yes/no | Peak throughput: <5k / 5k-50k / >50k tokens/min". That gives SDRs categories to pick in the gated form.
Maya: Also make the header shorter: "Secure inference: choose your deployment mode". And remove any weird characters (there's a stray control char in my view).
Nate: Approved on security text with the Compliance-Bot caveats. Add footnote: "Contact Sales for on-prem provisioning details; package varies by customer." Also add `@ops` to the final sign-off list.
Tom: I'll update and post a PDF by tomorrow AM. Owner: Tom. Reviewers: @Maya, @Ivy, @Nate, @ops. Timeline: Draft AM, final Friday EOD.
